rationale: This is a plain rank-product of two long-published anomalies (R&D-to-assets intensity à la Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis and cash-based profitability à la Novy-Marx/Ball et al.) with no gating or conditioning structure, so it is essentially a double-sort screen whose loading will be dominated by the profitability leg rather than any genuine interaction.

The two quantities have incommensurate units, so the ratio is mechanically dominated by the near-zero-volatility denominator (1/VOL blows up), meaning the signal will largely rediscover the known low-earnings-volatility/low-fundamental-risk premium rather than test intangible credibility, and a single winsorization pass will not fix that scaling pathology.

The quality leg is literally the negated Sloan (1996) total-accruals measure and the intangibles leg is close to the asset-growth/investment anomaly, so the product is a repackaging of two canonical anomalies whose expected positive sign will most plausibly be delivered by the accrual leg alone.

The trend in gross profit per dollar of R&D-plus-booked intangible capital is a genuinely non-standard construct rather than a relabeled known anomaly, though the reviewer should watch coverage loss from zero-intangible denominators and note that SUMRANK is additive and therefore weights, rather than truly gates, the stability channel claimed in the hypothesis.

The oancf/(dltt+dlc) gate divides by zero for debt-free firms, dropping exactly the safest self-funded innovators the hypothesis is about, and the arbitrary 0.5 threshold plus a [0,1] IND_RANK multiplier makes the sign flip depend on an unmotivated cut point with a large near-zero dead zone for low-R&D firms.

The short-side framing is coherent and the assets-scaled goodwill/intangible change avoids the degenerate-base problem, but the mechanism overlaps heavily with documented acquirer/goodwill-impairment underperformance and the quality leg is again accruals plus earnings volatility, so the negative slope is likely a rediscovery rather than a new interaction.
